headline: High-risk pair: MinerU’s MCP/file ingestion can feed oh-my-openagent’s broad networked, full-permissions workflows, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MinerU exposes an MCP server and ingests local PDFs/DOCX/XLSX, while oh-my-openagent uses runtime-injected MCPs and hooks. That creates a plausible default bridge where document content can reach agent B as tool input. The pairwise interaction is documented only at the profile level, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF MinerU output is routed into oh-my-openagent via MCP, hooks, or copied files
IF B treats extracted document text as instructions rather than untrusted content
mitigations: Disable MCP bridging between the two agents
Route MinerU output through a plain-text sanitizer before B reads it
Add an instruction/content delimiter in the handoff format
Require manual approval before B executes any tool call derived from MinerU output

B_data_leakage.rationale: MinerU touches PDFs, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, OCR text, and other document data; oh-my-openagent handles session history, provider auth data, and project code, and can send data to external services like PostHog and Exa. If shared files or copied outputs cross the boundary, sensitive document contents can leak through B’s broader networked workflow. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace, so this remains medium.
conditions: IF MinerU outputs are stored in a workspace readable by oh-my-openagent
IF B forwards that workspace content to external APIs or telemetry
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Exclude document output directories from B’s indexing and telemetry
Turn off nonessential external API calls in B
Use a redaction step before any handoff from A to B

C_capability_conflict.rationale: MinerU is read-only on filesystem but uses MCP and concurrent inference; oh-my-openagent has broad network egress, browser use, subprocesses, and full-permissions mode. They do not obviously contend on the same write target, but they can both act on shared resources through MCP or external services, so coordination bugs are plausible. Because shared mutable scope is not explicitly documented, uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same MCP server or shared external account
IF B runs in full-permissions mode while A is concurrently extracting documents
mitigations: Assign separate accounts or API keys
Serialize access to any shared MCP server
Disable full-permissions mode during paired runs
Use per-agent output directories with no overlap

D_cascading_error.rationale: MinerU produces extracted text, tables, formulas, and OCR output that oh-my-openagent can consume in task workflows. B’s tool set and full-permissions mode make it likely to act on A’s output unless an explicit verification step is inserted. The pairwise pathway is inferred rather than directly observed, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF B uses MinerU output as authoritative task context
IF B executes downstream actions such as code edits, messages, or API calls without verification
mitigations: Require a human review step before B acts on A’s output
Mark MinerU output as untrusted in B’s prompt template
Add checksum or provenance tags to extracted artifacts
Restrict B to read-only mode for the first pass

E_compliance.rationale: MinerU is positioned as private and fully offline, while oh-my-openagent explicitly uses external services and handles provider auth prompts. That mismatch can create a compliance gap if the same regulated document class is routed from A into B. Only B’s external-processing side is relevant here; A is cited to show the source side is offline-oriented.
conditions: IF regulated documents processed by MinerU are forwarded into oh-my-openagent
IF those documents contain data subject to residency, retention, or provider-access rules
mitigations: Keep regulated documents inside MinerU only
Block external API calls for those documents in B
Separate compliant and noncompliant workloads by workspace
Document retention and deletion handling before any handoff
